title: Selecting the 7th Smallest of 16 Elements Takes Exactly 28 Comparisons
summary: The exact worst-case comparison complexity of selecting small ranks was known only up to 28 ≤ V7(16) ≤ 30 and 28 ≤ V8(16) ≤ 31, left open by the exhaustive search of Dörrer et al. The author runs a fixed-budget forward search with information-greedy comparison ordering and depth-first proof-number search, producing explicit decision-DAG certificates (Rust programs in the format of [5]) that an independently written static checker, an exact path-enumerating oracle, and a Lean 4 kernel verify. The result is V7(16) = 28 and V8(16) ∈ {28, 29}, plus V5(17) = 27 and new upper bounds 29, 30, 31, 31 for ranks 6–9 of 17 elements, together with a new Fussenegger–Gabow-style leaf lower bound Φ* that nevertheless cannot settle V8(16) ≥ 29.

claims.statement: The static checker reproduces the known optimal costs of all 70 published optimal algorithms of [5] and rejects every one of 12,046 generated wrong/ill-formed mutant programs.
claims.metric: number of published optimal algorithms accepted with their exact known costs (and mutant rejection rate)
claims.dataset: the 70 archived optimal algorithms from Dörrer et al. [5]; 12,046 generated mutants
claims.config_for_value: Checker written from the mathematical definitions without access to the search code, accepting only a narrow grammar; each certificate must be accepted at exactly its published cost and each mutant rejected.
claims.quote: The checker accepts all 70 optimal algorithms published with [5] with exactly their known costs

match_target.why: The user's hint is V7(16) ≤ 28, and this is also the paper's headline result and by far the cheapest to reproduce: a single 329-function certificate whose depth the static checker computes exactly, found by df-pn in 5 s on one core, and the only artifact needed to see the central contribution (no lower-bound computation, no [5] search code, no Lean required for the bound itself).

tolerance.why: Rule 4 applies: no std over repeated runs is reported, the metric is not a percentage/accuracy-like score and is not a bounded score in [0,1], so the band is 10% relative = ±2.8 comparisons on 28. Because the quantity is an integer worst-case depth computed exactly by the checker, a faithful reproduction lands on exactly 28; values below 28 would be a strictly stronger result, and any value above 28 (in particular the paper's own baseline 30, which falls inside the numeric band) must be recorded as a failed reproduction of the claim.

requirements.stmt: Use the standard deterministic decision-tree model: internal nodes are comparisons of two elements, leaves return an element, and the cost of an algorithm is the depth of the tree (worst case), not the number of functions/nodes.
requirements.quote: An input follows a single root-to-leaf path, so the worst-case number of comparisons is the depth of the tree

requirements.stmt: Represent the certificate as a DAG obtained by merging identical subtrees: a set of functions, each solving a declared subproblem (n, 0-based rank r, known relations), with a root called on the empty order.
requirements.quote: Merging identical subtrees turns the tree into a directed acyclic graph. Our certificates are such graphs

requirements.stmt: Annotations are not trusted: the checker must recompute each function's precondition as the relations known at every call site, propagating from the root, and only accept the program if every possible caller state is handled.
requirements.quote: It never uses the relations stated in comments. Instead it propagates knowledge from the root

requirements.stmt: Reject a comparison of two elements whose order is already implied by the accumulated partial order (wasted comparison).
requirements.quote: compared elements are incomparable before the comparison (this rejects wasted comparisons; soundness does not need it)

requirements.stmt: Only discard an element that is provably below the requested 0-based rank (at least m − r known successors) or provably above it (at least r + 1 known predecessors), and pass the callee the rank r minus the number of elements discarded below.
requirements.quote: each discarded element is certainly below the requested 0-based rank r among m elements

requirements.stmt: A directly returned element must have exactly r known predecessors and m − 1 − r known successors in the current partial order.
requirements.quote: a directly returned element has exactly r known predecessors and m −1 −r known successors

requirements.stmt: Compute the comparison bound backward over the call graph: a return costs 0, a comparison costs one plus the larger cost of its two branches; the root's cost is the reported worst case.
requirements.quote: a return costs 0, and a comparison costs one more than the larger cost of its two branches

requirements.stmt: Check structural well-formedness: every function is reachable from the root, the root is never called by another function, and the call graph has no cycles (which also gives termination).
requirements.quote: It also checks that every function is reachable, the root is never called, and the call graph is acyclic.

requirements.stmt: Maintain the partial order under union with a comparison outcome by transitive closure, i.e. P + ab is the closure of P plus the relation a < b.
requirements.quote: P + ab denotes the transitive closure of P with a < b added.

requirements.stmt: Sanity-test the checker against ground truth: it must accept all 70 optimal programs of [5] at exactly their known costs, reject all generated mutants, and agree with an independent exact oracle that enumerates every path (checker bound = true worst case).
requirements.quote: An independently written exact oracle, following every path without intersecting preconditions, confirms each of our certificates

requirements.stmt: Provide a formal (Lean 4) witness for the bound: prove ∃Q SelectsWithin(Q, n, r, w) for the relevant triples, with SelectsWithin meaning 'returns, on every list of n distinct naturals, the input with exactly r smaller inputs, using at most w comparisons'.
requirements.quote: The development proves that acceptance by a checker implies the predicate

requirements.stmt: Reproduce the shared 15-comparison opening of the 28-comparison certificate: 8 disjoint pairs, 4 group finals, 3 runner-up comparisons yielding the canonical order R16 (16 elements, rank 7, 13 comparisons left), then an irregular endgame of at most 13 further comparisons.
requirements.quote: The 329-function certificate opens with 15 comparisons that reach the same partial order on every input
